Mr. Miljanovic, we, the four judges up here, have no idea at all what questions will be put to you and by whom, except that we know for sure that the Defence teams for General Miletic will surely be asking -- putting some questions to you, but they will be followed by others. And we do not exclude, because we cannot, that there might be some questions which, if you answer truthfully, could possibly expose you to possible criminal proceedings. I don't know, I am not tell you that this will be the case, because as I said I don't know what questions will be asked. But if you feel that by answering truthfully any particular question, you may be incriminating yourself, you have a right to draw our attention to that and ask that you be exempted from answering such a question. This is not an absolute right. We have the option and the right to grant you such exemption, but we can also decide to deny your request and order you to answer such questions. If we order you to answer such questions, you have a further right under our rules and that is that whatever you may say in replying to such incriminatory questions, cannot be made use of later on in any proceedings that may be taken against you, criminal proceedings, that may be taken against you by this Tribunal or elsewhere. Unless, of course, in answering such questions you are rendering yourself responsible for perjury. Is that clear enough to you? Have I explained myself well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think Ms. Fauveau will go first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, could you tell us your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my name is Ratko Miljanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What's your educational background, what sort of schools have you finished?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the secondary technical school in Gradanska?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In construction, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then the military technical academy, the command staff tactical school, and the school for national defence, those are the schools that I have graduated from.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What position did you hold before the war in the former Yugoslavia broke out?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war in the former Yugoslavia broke out, I was the chief of the military gymnasium, Ivolola Ribar in the Yugoslav Peoples' Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And before holding that position --

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before that when graduating from the military technical academy, I was the command of the platoon for technical maintenance and for technical supplies, I was also an official for the technical department in an infantry regiment. Then, I was the deputy company commander for technical maintenance of technical equipment. It was in a logistic organ and in a very large barracks. And then I was the commander of a platoon in the school for reserve officers who were within the technical service of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. And then I was the chief of a class in the military technical academy for the land army, the territorial army, the land forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were located when you were performing all the duties that you mentioned in your last question -- in your last answer?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The first position I mentioned, that of a platoon company in the position of the deputy commander for the maintenance service, well, those duties I performed in Skopje. And then duties I performed in the military technical academy when I had the position as head of the Ivolola Ribar gymnasium, on those occasions, I was located in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Have you ever served in Serbia? Did you ever serve in Serbia between -- before 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Where were you when the war in the former Yugoslavia broke out?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Zagreb. I was the head of the military secondary school, Ivolola Ribar.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And how did you leave Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, after our barracks in Zagreb had been under blockade for three months, I left with a column of vehicles and men. It was a column of the -- from the military technical school of the land forces of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. And this column set off from the Zagreb to Karlovac, Banja Luka, Belgrade; and I then arrived in Krusevac in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said that you were under a three-month blockade. Did you have any contact with the outside world during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, during that period of time, and particularly towards the end of that period, we had minimal contact which was under surveillance. But otherwise, we had no communications, movement was restricted, food and water wasn't supplied.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And one last question about this subject, who else was with you in the barracks during those three months?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the barracks there were 13 professional officers who remained towards the end of that period, and there were 50 soldiers who remained there. They were serving their military service, that's a total of 63 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What position did you hold after having managed to leave Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was appointed as commander of the secondary military technical schools of the land forces. At the time it was already within the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: During this period, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior officer was the late General Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was General Djukic your immediate superior during the entire period of time that you spent in Serbia or did this change at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. He was my immediate superior until I left the army of -- until leaving to the army of Republika Srpska, somewhere around May 1992. And of afterwards, my immediate superior was -- General, or maybe a colonel I can't remember at the time, Ratomir Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When did you join the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I joined the army of Republika Srpska on the 26th of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And why did you decide the join the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was born in Bosnia and Herzegovina. My mother still lives in my place of birth, as well as my closest relatives, and I was sent from Bosnia, from my place of birth, to attend military schools.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What positions did you hold in the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, from the beginning until the end of my service in the army of Republika Srpska, I held position of the chief of the department for operations and logistics. It was within the logistics section of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And who was your immediate superior in the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior in the army of Republika Srpska was General Djukic. Apart from when I represented him and performed his duties, on that occasion my immediate superior was General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We'll go back to that periods a little later. You mentioned General Mladic. Did you know General Mladic before joining the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I met General Mladic in a unit I had been assigned to having graduated from the military technical academy in Skopje in 1970. We served together up until 1977.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I met General Miletic when I arrived in the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What position did General Miletic hold in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: General Miletic was the chief of operations and training within the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in 1995 who was the chief of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the Main Staff of the army Republika Srpska was General Milovanovic, Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know where General Milovanovic was in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: General Milovanovic, in the summer of 1995, was involved in an operation in Bosnian Krajina, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And who was the chief of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska when General Milovanovic was in Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: General Milovanovic was always the chief of the Main Staff. I never met anyone else who held that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: During this period in the summer of 1995, did you have any contact with General Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. I did have contact with him on occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would now like to go into more details with regard to the position that you held. You said that you stood in for General Djukic for a certain period of time, but before doing that who would replace General Djukic when he was absent?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: When General Djukic was absent, and in performing daily duties at the logistics command post, and in the sector for logistics of the Main Staff, I would stand in for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I should like to show you a document showing the structure of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is document P3178. Unfortunately, it is a Prosecution document which has not been translated into English. Can we have page 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What we can see at the bottom of this page. Sir, I know that this is not a good copy, but does the end of this page actually relate to the logistics section?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is the sector for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And here we see the name of Djordje Djukic.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go to the next page, page 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you see your name on this page?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do see my name.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And just before your name, one can see the word "colonel," and also the head and also the deputy assistant for logistics. What does this mean at the same time, "deputy assistant"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it says here in the first column: "The organ for operation and logistics affairs." And then after that, "(chief also deputy assistant commander for logistics)." And then in the next column headed "rank," it says "colonel." And then in the next column, "family," father's name and first name. And in the second line it says, "Milijanovic, Tose, Ratko." That's me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain what is in brackets, also deputy commander -- deputy assistant commander for logistics. What does this mean, could you explain what that means, please?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I shall try to explain in the way it was explained to me and how I understood my duty at the time. If, as was my case, my position was the chief and at the same time deputy assistant commander for logistics, this means that I, who was appointed to this position, may deputize for the deputy commander for logistics in the performances his daily duties when he is physically absent at the command post for logistics. Also, that I may stand in for him with all the authority and responsibility that is assigned to him with his position during the time when he is prevented from performing his duties due to; for instance, sickness, official travel, annual leave, and the like. And if that absence doesn't last longer than one month. That is what this means.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've already said that you represented General Djukic. Could you explain the situations in which you stood in for General Djukic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stood in for General Djukic in the sense in which I have just explained when he was prevented from performing his duties. And this happened on a number of occasions for short periods of time when he would officially travel to Serbia, or somewhere else, I didn't know where. And that is when I would stand in for him in performing his daily duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you deputize for General Djukic for a longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was there a period when General Djukic was sick?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In the period from the end of March until the beginning of June 1995, General Djukic could not perform his duty because of illness and surgery and treatment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what was your function during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, I performed my regular duties. And by a decision of the command of the Main Staff, an order was written for me to stand in for General Djukic, and I was appointed to that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What was the importance of that order, the order whereby you were appointed?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, by this appointment, I was given the inalienable right to decide about the use of effectives and materiel subordinated to the assistant -- main commander for logistics, and also I had to bear responsibility for any consequences that may arise as a result of such use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's time for the for the break whenever it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have one more question on this subject, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you obtain any personal privileges as a result of this order, or benefits?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. As opposed to the period when I stood in, sort of automatically, for the General, when I represented him my salary increased. I don't remember for how much. The difference being between the salary that belonged to my position and the position held by General Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we can now have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what we will do. 25 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should just like to clear up the subject that we discussed with respect to document B3038 [as interpreted], that we discussed with the previous witness. I have spoken to the Prosecutor, and he agrees that it -- that the document comes from the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. We are not challenging it, and I just wish -- I just wish to tell you that the document came from Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's bring in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, before the break, we were talking about situations when General Djukic was prevented from exercising his duties. What was the situation when General Djukic was not at his post in Han Pijesak, but he was nevertheless somewhere in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Djukic would frequently be absent from the command post for logistics performing other documents, in most cases in the field. In those cases all subordinate organs in the sector for logistics performed their duties in accordance with the duties and in accordance with the instructions that he gave them from time to time. Therefore, in addition to my regular duties, I would also takeover some of his, and that meant receiving visitors, taking care of the duty officers at the command post for logistics, reviewing the documents in the mail, signing documents which should have been signed by him, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you signed documents for General Djukic, how did you sign them?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, that is, shortly after I joined the army of Republika Srpska, this matter was not really regulated. General Djukic had not defined it, so that frequently we would put the word "for," and then at a certain point in time he decided that this should not be done any longer, and he instructed his subordinates that each person should sign documents from their sphere of responsibility. And if I signed documents that he should have signed, I would have to put "deputy" or the word "representing" and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when General Djukic was not in Han Pijesak and documents arrived which needed to be responded to, if there was a request that arrived or something, what would happen? Who would take the decision?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Djukic had, I can say, a permanent communication with the command post; and, therefore, with me too, so I would regularly inform him about the most important questions that needed to be dealt with while -- during his physical absence from the command post. General Djukic, as a rule, gave instructions how a particular order should be written, what the content should be, and he virtually dictated such documents. And his decision was always there. It was always present.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was it possible for you to decide when General Djukic was somewhere else in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be in contradiction with the basic principle of single command, which applied in the armies I served in and also contrary to the rules that I studied. So that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who could issue orders to General Djukic within the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The immediate superior to General Djukic was the command of the Main Staff, General Mladic, and he was the only one who could issue him orders. He was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In certain conditions, could someone else in the army of Republika Srpska give orders to General Djukic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Only in the event that the commander of the Main Staff was prevented from performing his duties and if someone else was standing in his place, that is, the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the Chief of Staff, please?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already said that the Chief of Staff was General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Have you had -- did you have opportunity to hear General Milovanovic giving orders to General Djukic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did attend one such conversation. I was present there. General Milovanovic called General Djukic and said something to him, I didn't hear what, and then General Djukic in my presence answered: "General, I am not your subordinate. And remember once and for all that you cannot order me around."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Where was the logistics centre of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska headquartered?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am afraid I didn't get a good translation. I assume the question is where the command post was. Could you please kindly repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The logistics sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of the Main Staff, Madam Fauveau? The logistics centre of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The logistics centre of the Main Staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the VRS. The logistics sector.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The logistic sector of the Main Staff was deployed at the rear command post of the VRS in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What other sectors and organs of the army of Republika Srpska were based in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the logistics sector and within the framework of the rear command post, there were also the following organs: The sector for organisation, mobilization, and personnel affairs; a part of the organ for moral, religious, and legal affairs; I think that's what its name was, part of that sector; then the supreme court-martial and the prosecutor's office; the communications unit; and the encryption unit; also the department for air and technical security; a part of the organ for finances, and I hope I've listed all of them. I may I have left some of them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain for us the structure of the logistics centre? What elements constituted the logistics sector?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get a time-frame? Because this is a long period of time that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In 1995, to avoid any confusion, when you spoke about the organs that were in Han Pijesak which period were you referring to? During which period were these organs, these bodies, present there?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I meant the entire period throughout which I was staying at the rear command post between January 1993 and the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you now tell us what the structure of the logistics sector was like in 1995, the logistics sector of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the logistics sector, it breaks down in the following way: The Department for Operations and Logistics, and I was the one who headed that department, it's a department that we mentioned already. There was the Technical Department, there was the Quarter Masters' Department, there was a Traffic Department, there was a Medical Department, there was a Veterinarian Department, and there was a Construction Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what did the section for operations and logistics look like? What were the tasks of the sector for logistics and operations?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpretation that I am receiving is the sector for operations and logistics. I suppose the references is to the department; therefore, the department for operations and logistics had its tasks prescribed. Drafting plans for supporting units of the army of Republika Srpska in terms of logistic was one of those. This also required an ongoing updating procedure. Further, monitoring the operating of the logistics system of the army of Republika Srpska. Further, proposing measures to improve its work and to make it more functional. Further, activities to do with organising and implementing the fire protection programme, protection at workplace and protection of the environment in which we were staying. We were also supposed to monitor the combat readiness of the units and institutions subordinate to the logistics head. And also proposing measures to improve that. Further, participating in the production of the plan -- logistical plan, for any operations planned and carried out by the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska. Further, controlling the units and institutions of the logistics department, participating in the organisation and implementation of the monitoring [as interpreted] procedure that applied to combat readiness of the units of the army Republika Srpska as a whole. As well as carrying out any other tasks or jobs ordered by the superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: With regard to the transcript, page 70, line 12 -- 17, we can see the word "monitoring" appear, did you say to "monitor" or to "follow"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: I said "following."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How many subordinates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think in the English that roughly means the same thing, so if we are talking about -- and I know this is going from French, but could we get a B/C/S word, because as you may recall "monitoring" is a word used frequently in the indictment, but it's meant in the normal English sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Madam Fauveau, I wasn't following you in French I was following the translation, which word did you use in French?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I used the words "surveillez" and "suivre." It's the difference between these two words. Perhaps this should be clarified once and for all. Perhaps this could be done tomorrow without the witness being present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You agree to that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, but if we could use the Serbian words I think we would be better off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And which would be the Serbian word? Is that a -- is there a unitary word, single word for both concepts or do you still have to use two?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness perhaps take his headset off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you remove your headset for a moment, Mr. Miljanovic. And she will be using a word which probably isn't B/C/S which we will understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, I'd like to clarify this a little more, the word "monitor" used in English is translated as "surveillance" in French; and it's translated as "nadzer" or "nadgledanje" in B/C/S. The word, "suivre," which means following is "pracinje [phoen]" in B/C/S, and the witness used the word "pracinje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did I use the other one as well, the one which would reflect "surveillance" or "surveillez."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, no, Mr. President, he didn't, but I can ask the witness to clear the matter up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't know how the indictment got translated. When we said "monitoring" which word it was given, but it was meant in -- not in -- in monitoring, I believe from what I'm hearing, may be in the term that one of the Yugoslav terms, it may be a military term; and I just -- to clarify the indictment is not meant "monitoring" as a Yugoslav military term, it's meant to "follow" or to "monitor." It's common lawyer English, if there is such a thing; and so this distinction that's being made is really of no distinction. We are not -- the indictment is not meant to be based on a Yugoslav military model.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, okay, let's stop here on this and if necessary we will take it up again tomorrow. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that this is a very serious question, because the accused has the indictment in B/C/S and the word used there is a translation of the word "surveillance" into B/C/S. If you change the indictment, well, then our Defence case should change, too. That's fine with me, but we then have to have a break, have a pause in this case, and we would have to prepare ourselves again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey didn't like that. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We could all quit and come back in January, but that's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we won't be the first to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. As Ms. Fauveau knows, Serbian is not an official language of the -- of the Tribunal, it's -- perhaps it should have been, but what they are looking at is the Tribunal's -- the CLSS's best guide on what that means. Now, French is, so we may go get into a battle battles over French in this issue, but we should not be in a battle over Serbian, and I will have to bring in Ms. Soljan to help me out on the battle for French, but I think we can see the issue. But I think it's - as you say - a tempest in a teapot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed, and if we need to come back to this, we will. He can put on the headset again. Mr. Miljanovic, have you been following what we were saying in English and in French?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know French or English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, when you answered my question, did you at any point in time use the word "surveillance, surveillez," "monitor"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I didn't use that term. I ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How many subordinates did you ever in your department in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, within my department, there was a single post that was filled, and that was me; therefore, I did not have a single subordinate under me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know how many people should have been working in your department? According to the army structure, the army booklet on staff composition, how many staff members should there have been in your department?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my job in my career, I never dealt with those issues that had to do with the organisation or establishment; nevertheless, based on the name itself, on the term "department," what that means in our terminology, is roughly a squat, about ten people plus a head. The sheer scope of that department's job would corroborate that figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned the tasks that your department had. Can you tell us what tasks the technical department had?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The technical department was in charge of a subsystem of logistics support, we call it technical support, in our army. So they were in charge of this subsystem as it were. Fundamentally, their tasks would be as follows -- I can't be expected to enumerate all of those. They were there to supply equipment and material. They were in charge of maintenance as well. They were supposed to supply those forms of energy and fuel, stationery and other disposables or spare parts in the case of equipment. Those would be their paramount tasks, and I can't think of any other ones right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Which department was responsible for ammunition?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The technical department, didn't I say that? Ammunition, mines, explosives, they were in charge of all of these.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was the position of commander of logistics a position that had a duty post that was organised? Was there a duty post in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not sure I understand the question fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What don't you understand of it? The question as we have it at least in our transcript is the following: "Was the position of commander of logistics a position that had a duty post that was organised? Was there a duty post for commander of logistics in Han Pijesak?" We need to know what you don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There is no commander of logistics is one problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but this is what I was reading what we have in the transcript. Ms. Fauveau, if you could rephrase your question, we would be happy to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was there a post, a duty officer post, in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've understood the question. There was at the rear command post, and it was called the Operations Duty Officer at the Rear Command Post.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Which officers occupied the post of duty officer at this command post, this logistics command post?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: This position was occupied by officers from all the various structures deployed at the rear command post apart from communications detachment, but they had shifts, they were all engaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did officers from logistics sector have duty officers at the Crna Rijeka command post?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a while. There were a number of officers who were posted to the rear command post, and they continued to exercise their duties there in Han Pijesak. But then they were resubordinated to operations duties in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you tell us, with regard to General Djukic, could give orders as assistant for logistics? To whom could General Djukic give orders?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: General Djukic could give orders to all of his subordinate officers within the sector as well as units and institutions that were subordinated to him. Under the rules of command - I am not sure if my term is right - as assistant commander of the Main Staff of the army Republika Srpska, he could - at least in terms of logistics - also exercise command over corps and other units of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would first of all like to discuss in the subject of subordinate units. Which units were subordinate ones in the logistics sector of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The assistant for logistics at the rear bases that were subordinate to him. There was also the vehicle transportation battalion, the military hospital, the military medical centre at Banja Luka, the Krajina military institution, the overhaul at Kosmos, the Orao overhaul unit, the Hadzici overhaul unit, the automatic data processing centre, I guess that's what the name was, anyway it was in Banja Luka, the military book keeping centre. I think that one was there too. That would be it for the most part. I may I have omitted one or two whose names escape me right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned an auto battalion, do you know where this battalion was located?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that. The vehicle or auto battalion, when I first arrived in the army of Republika Srpska, was somewhere near Sokolac. It was stationed in that area. At a later stage, it was moved to a location near Zvornik. There was a factory there, whose name I can't remember, but it was stationed within the factory compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did these subordinate units, subordinate to the logistics sector, send daily reports?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of the units subordinated to General Djukic submitted regular combat reports, and this applied to all the other army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And to whom were these reports addressed?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: The reports came directly from these units to General Djukic at the rear command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now I would like to clarify something that you said a minute ago, page 77, line 4 and line 5. You said that with regard to logistics, General Djukic could give the corps orders. Could you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I said that, what I meant was this: General Djukic, regarding any issues that had to do with the logistics support or any issues regarding -- what shall I call them? Instructions, procedures on procedures, he had the power to prescribe rules in relation to these for the entire army and also to order -- order the implementation thereof. By way of an example, instructions on the storing and handling of ammunition and explosives. He could have issued an order on that and all the units would have been duty-bound to implement and follow his instructions. So this would be an example of a logistics job where he had the power to give orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any time it's convenient, unless you have further questions on this sector?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two minor questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the corps send reports to the logistics sector?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of the corps including the airforce and the airforce command submitted to the rear command post what we refer to as a logistics report -- or, rather, a report to the logistics support.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you like, we could stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Fauveau. Mr. Miljanovic, we are going to stop here for today. We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime between now and tomorrow please do not allow anyone to communicate with you or you discuss with anyone the subject matters of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
